subject: SLA credit request follow-up: outage on 2027-02-24 (CygnusAI)
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cygnusai.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <asha@cygnusai.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request for SLA credit after 2027-02-24 outage

Diego,

Thanks again for the incident write-up yesterday. Our engineering and legal teams reviewed the timeline and we believe CygnusAI is entitled to a service credit under section 4.2 of the SLA — the outage caused ~3.1 hours of degraded responses across our core inference pool (production region us-west-2).

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood agrees this qualifies for a credit?
- The exact calculation you will apply (per-token vs per-hour; lookback window)
- Expected timeline for issuance and whether this will appear as a credit on our next invoice or a one-time refund?

We attached our internal impact summary for reference (short). Appreciate a concrete proposal so we can close the loop with procurement.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure, CygnusAI
(sanjay@cygnusai.com)

Attachments: cygnus_impact_summary.pdf (6 pages)

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cygnusai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit after 2027-02-24 outage

Sanjay — thanks for sending the summary and for the quick review on your side. Short answers up front:

- We acknowledge the incident and are treating this as eligible for a credit under the SLA.
- I'm running a detailed calculation with Billing; preliminary approach attached (spreadsheet). We compute credits based on the impacted capacity window and the monthly committed units for Dedicated customers. If you are on metered/hosted pricing we'll apply the hosted per-token offset approach — I'll call out both scenarios in the calc.
- Issuance: we can either apply a one-time invoice credit (recommended) or a refund. Typical turnaround is 7–10 business days after approval.

I'll loop in Monica (Billing) and Marissa (Customer Success) to confirm numbers and approve issuance. Expect a follow-up with line-item math today.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Diego Fernandez | Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_calculation_2027-02-24.xlsx (draft)

From: monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cygnusai.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit after 2027-02-24 outage

Hi all — Monica from Billing here. I reviewed Diego's draft calc and ran our standard procedure for Dedicated customers. Summary of steps we followed (attached workbook contains line items):

1) Verified incident window per the incident timeline (2027-02-24 01:15–05:40 UTC) and mapped to impacted deployment nodes.
2) Computed hourly equivalence of committed units impacted (Committed GPU-hours prorated).
3) Applied SLA credit percentage per contract tier (10% per hour beyond SLO threshold in this case).
4) Converted the credit amount to invoice units (USD) and prepared both a credit memo and an optional refund entry.

Result (draft): $18,450 credit. Breakdown in attachment. This assumes CygnusAI accepts the invoice-credit option. If you prefer a cash refund, we can do that but it will take an extra 3–5 business days to process.

Sanjay — please confirm acceptance of the invoice credit and whether you'd like us to proceed.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cygnusai_incident_timeline_20270224.csv, credit_calculation_2027-02-24.xlsx

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cygnusai.com>
To: monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <asha@cygnusai.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 07:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit after 2027-02-24 outage

Monica — thanks for the quick calc and transparency. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign off:

1) The $18,450 figure — can you share the hourly rate and the exact number of impacted committed GPU-hours you used? We want to reconcile to our invoices.
2) Does the calculation net any previously applied usage discounts or promotional credits? Please show gross and net values.
3) For the timeline you used, we recorded several degraded requests until 07:30 UTC (some fallbacks to smaller models). Can you confirm whether the window you used included the degraded-but-still-serving period or only full downtime?

We prefer the invoice credit option. If you can provide the two-line reconciliation, we'll acknowledge and you can proceed with the credit memo.

Best,
Sanjay

On a separate note — thanks to Diego and Marissa for the rapid postmortem. The remediation plan looks good; we'll retest in two weeks and update you if we see repeat regressions.

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cygnusai.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit after 2027-02-24 outage

Sanjay — following up with the reconciliation you requested. Monica and I reviewed the items and updated the workbook. Key reconciliation points (also in the attached final calc):

- Impact window used: 2027-02-24 01:15–06:10 UTC. We included the degraded-serving tail (the period where requests were routed to smaller model variants and latency exceeded the SLO) because the SLA clause references degraded availability, not only full outages.
- Impacted committed GPU-hours: 124.5 GPU-hours (prorated across the Dedicated pool you have in us-west-2). Hourly equivalent rate applied: $148.50 per GPU-hour (effective committed rate after discounts).
- Gross credit before applied promotions: $18,493.25. We then netted the promotional discount applied to the billing account, resulting in the final credit memo amount: $18,450.00. Line-by-line reconciliation is sheet 'reconciliation' in the workbook.

Action requested: Please reply to this thread with a one-line approval ("Approve invoice credit $18,450") and we'll generate a credit memo and apply it to your next invoice. Once applied, Finance will send a confirmation and updated invoice PDF.

Thanks for working through this with us. If you prefer a different treatment we can pivot.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_calculation_2027-02-24-final.xlsx (final)
